titulo: Step 1: from chat to the terminal (OSWork)
lead: The terminal is just another window. With six commands, you can move through your folders; with an AGENTS.md, the agent knows who you are and what it can do; with Git, you can undo any mistake.
objetivo: set up the agent’s work folder with rules, a safety net, and secrets kept out of the text.

aprende.t: Move through folders in the terminal
Keep keys out of the text

secoes.sub: You give the task, the agent works inside the folder, and you review it.

nos.detalhe: You’re still the one who decides: you ask, review the result, and accept or undo it. Giving the task, reviewing, and deciding is management.

nos.sub: cmd, Mac Terminal, or Linux terminal
nos.detalhe: This is how you get to the folder and call the agent. On Windows, use cmd; on Mac and Linux, use the Terminal.
Everything the agent needs to know goes here: the rules in AGENTS.md, the work in the files, the keys in .env (which Git ignores), and the history in .git.
The agent reads AGENTS.md before starting, works on the files in the folder, and, if the rules require it, says what changed and how you can review it.

secoes.volta: Not happy with it? git restore returns the file to the last saved version
secoes.legenda: The same files work for Claude Code and Codex: both read AGENTS.md.

rolagem_fim.texto: You ask, the agent works inside the folder following AGENTS.md, and says what changed. You review it. If you like it, commit; if not, use git restore.

secoes.titulo: The work cycle with the agent

texto: Inside the folder, run claude or codex and ask for one thing, with the result you expect.
Start by asking it to read AGENTS.md so it follows your rules.

exemplo.texto: Read AGENTS.md. Create an index.html with a simple page about me, using the information there.

texto: The agent creates and edits files in the folder. It may ask permission before running commands.
Your role here is to read what it proposes, not type for it.

exemplo.texto: The agent creates index.html and explains what it did.

texto: Open the result (the page in your browser, the summary, or the file) and compare it with what you asked for.
Ask for at least one correction: that’s the habit that separates using from managing.

exemplo.texto: Change the title to "HR Consulting" and add a contact section.

texto: Like it? git add . and git commit -m "..." save the version.
Don’t like it? git restore index.html restores the saved version. No panic.

exemplo.texto: Make a commit before asking for a big change.

secoes.titulo: The files and commands in this sequence
secoes.sub: Copy and use them. Replace the text between the < > signs with your own.

blocos.conteudo:
mkdir projetos
cd projetos
mkdir meu-primeiro-agente
cd meu-primeiro-agente
dir      # Windows (on Mac and Linux: ls)

# Who I am
<your name, your profession, who you work for>

# Rules for this project
- Write in Portuguese, using short sentences.
- Don’t delete files without asking.
- Before finishing, say what changed and how I can check it.
- Never write keys or passwords in a text file; they belong in .env.

# What’s here
- index.html: my page

blocos.rot: Terminal · Git and keeping secrets out of text
blocos.conteudo:
git init
echo .env> .gitignore
git add .
git commit -m "primeira versão"

# undo an agent's change:
git restore index.html

# .env must NOT appear here:
git status

abas.html:
1. You can reach the folder using only the terminal and say which folder you’re in.
  2. AGENTS.md has at least three rules you wrote.
  3. The page opens in your browser, and you asked for at least one correction.
  4. git status does not show .env.

• Skipping Git: the agent’s first bad change means manual rework.
  • Key in AGENTS.md: anything in plain text could end up on GitHub. Keep keys only in .env.
  • Vague request: "improve the page" leads to changes you don’t know how to check. Ask for a result you can see.

secoes.sub: Do them in order. Move on only when the "done when" condition is true.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · First folder using the terminal
exercicios.texto: Create projetos/meu-primeiro-agente, go into it, and list its contents. Open the same folder in File Explorer (or Finder) and compare.
exercicios.pronto: you can reach the folder using only the terminal, without the mouse, and say which folder you’re in.

exercicios.texto: Create AGENTS.md with who you are, the project rules, and what’s in the folder.
exercicios.pronto: the file exists and has at least three rules that you wrote yourself.

exercicios.texto: Call the agent and ask it to create index.html based on AGENTS.md. Open it in your browser and ask for a change.
exercicios.pronto: the page opens, and you asked the agent for at least one correction.

exercicios.texto: Run git init, add, and commit. Ask for a big change, and if you don’t like it, revert it with git restore.
exercicios.pronto: you undid an agent’s change with one command, no panic.

exercicios.titulo: E5 · Keep secrets out of the text
exercicios.texto: Create a .env file with a fake key and a .gitignore file with the line .env. Add the rule to AGENTS.md.

exercicios.titulo: E6 · The agent reads your files
exercicios.texto: Put three of your own texts in the folder and ask for a resumo.md with 5 decisions and 5 open items, citing the source of each one.
exercicios.pronto: you found at least two of the quoted sentences in the original.

secoes.fonte: Complete exercises, including the extra challenge (repeat with the other agent): jornada-agentes/exercicios/01-oswork.md.

secoes.sub: Six commands, one AGENTS.md, and the first task.
The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Where does an API key go in a project?
opcoes: In AGENTS.md, so the agent knows how to use it.
perguntas.explica: Keep the key only in .env, and put .env in .gitignore. That way, git status won’t show the file, and it won’t go to GitHub.

perguntas.p: The agent made a big change you didn’t approve. What should you do?
opcoes: Delete the folder and start over.
Ask the agent to try to remember how it was.
Run git restore on the file to return it to the last saved version.
Copy the old file from a manual backup.
perguntas.explica: With a commit made before the change, git restore returns the file to its previous state in one command. That’s why the rule is: commit before asking for a big change.

opcoes: It’s the manual the agent reads before working: who you are, the rules, and what’s in the folder.
perguntas.explica: AGENTS.md is the employee handbook. Claude Code and Codex read the same file, so the rules apply to both.
